title: Third-loop htr — the camel stitch
subtitle: Insert into the hidden loop behind the htr top to make a knit-like rib
excerpt: Third-loop htr inserts into the horizontal bar sitting at the back of every htr's top, rather than the usual two top loops. This third loop is invisible from the front. Working into it creates a flat knit-like rib and is the stitch behind the 'camel stitch' and moss-stitch crochet effect.

glossaryTerms.definition: A half treble worked by inserting into the horizontal bar at the back of the previous row's htr top instead of the usual two loops. Creates a flat, knit-like rib. Also called camel stitch or camel htr.

heroPrompt: A crochet swatch in warm grey DK yarn showing 6 rows of third-loop htr (camel stitch), the flat knit-like rib texture visible clearly, close-up side view.

inlineDiagramTopics.description: The back of an htr top showing the third horizontal bar, with hook positioned to insert into it

content.text: uses a loop that most crocheters never notice. Every htr top has three strands: the usual two loops you see from the front, and a third horizontal bar that runs across the back. Inserting into this hidden bar leaves the two front loops free to sit on top of the work as a visible ridge — the same effect as knit rib, but made entirely with a crochet hook.

attrs.title: Finding the third loop
attrs.body: Hold the work with the right side facing you and tilt the top edge slightly away. The third loop is the horizontal strand running along the back of the top of each htr — it sits below the two top loops and slightly behind them. It looks like the 'purl bump' on a knit stitch.

content.text: Work a foundation row of standard htr.
Turn. Ch 2. Tilt the top edge slightly toward you to expose the back of the previous row's htr tops.
Insert the hook into the third loop only — the horizontal bar at the back of the first htr. Both front loops of that htr stay visible on the fabric surface.
Yarn over, draw up a loop (3 loops on hook), yarn over, pull through all 3 loops — one third-loop htr made.
Continue into the third loop of each htr across the row.

items.cause: Looking at the top edge head-on rather than tilting the work
items.fix: Tilt the row edge slightly away from you or hold the work sideways under good light. The third loop sits lower and behind the main two loops.

items.cause: The third-loop htr creates a denser fabric than standard htr by design
items.fix: Go up one hook size if the rib is stiffer than wanted, or use a lighter weight yarn. The rib effect is maximised on DK and above.

content.text: Front-post and back-post double crochet (FPDC and BPDC) produce a similar rib by working around the post of the stitch rather than into the top. Post stitches give a deeper, more pronounced rib and are standard for crochet cables.
